page.title: Routing Rules
page.description: Manage routing rules to control how requests are routed across providers

rules.title: Routing Rules
rules.enableRuleDescription: Rule will be active and applied to matching requests
rules.chainRuleDescription: After this rule matches, re-evaluate routing rules using the resolved provider/model as the new context. Useful for composing rules, e.g. normalize a model alias first, then route based on the canonical name.
rules.priorityHint: Lower numbers = higher priority (0 is highest)
rules.routingTargetRequired: At least one routing target is required
rules.targetWeightMustBePositive: Each target weight must be greater than 0
rules.targetWeightsMustSumToOne: Target weights must sum to 1, current total: {{total}}
rules.noRulesDesc: Create your first routing rule to get started
rules.name: Name
rules.deleteRuleConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete "{{name}}"? This action cannot be undone.
rules.readMoreAriaLabel: Read more about routing rules (opens in new tab)

sheet.createDescription: Create a new routing rule with conditions
sheet.ruleBuilderDesc: Build conditions to determine when this rule should apply. Leave empty to apply this rule to all requests.
sheet.budgetNote: Note: Ensure token limits, request limits, and budget are configured in <1>Model Providers → Configurations → {provider} → Governance</1> (provider-level) or <3>Model Providers → Budgets & Limits</3> section (model-level) before using them in routing rules.
sheet.routingTargetsDesc: Weights must sum to 1. Leave provider or model empty to use the incoming request value.
sheet.fallbacksDesc: Provider is required, but model is optional. Leave model empty to use the incoming request value.
sheet.fallbacksOrder: Fallbacks will be used in the order they are defined
sheet.emptyExpressionHelper: Leave empty to match all requests.
sheet.virtualModelHint: Use "==" or "in [ ... ]" for the model field so this virtual model appears in /v1/models. Other operators still match at request time, but won't show up in the model catalog.
sheet.switchToBuilderDesc: The visual builder can't import a hand-written expression, so your current expression will be discarded and the builder will start empty. Copy it first if you want to keep it.

ruleBuilderEmptyState.title: No match conditions yet
ruleBuilderEmptyState.subtitle: This rule will match every request. Pick an example to start, or click Add Rule below.
ruleBuilderEmptyState.builderInfo: Leave blank to match every request. Use the visual Builder for most cases; switch to Expression mode for advanced conditions.
ruleBuilderEmptyState.toggleHint: Switch to Expression mode to write conditions directly.
ruleBuilderEmptyState.helper: You can edit or remove the inserted rule after.

fieldDescription.model: Match requests by the requested model name. Supports exact values, lists, contains, prefix/suffix, and regex patterns.
fieldDescription.provider: Match requests by the upstream provider handling them.
fieldDescription.request_type: Filter rules by the type of API request (chat, text, embeddings, images, audio, etc.). Streaming and non-streaming requests are distinct types: select both to cover all requests of a kind.
fieldDescription.complexity_tier: Route by the complexity category assigned by the Complexity Router (Simple, Medium, Complex, or Reasoning).
fieldDescription.has_image: Match requests whose body contains at least one image block (image_url in chat completions, input_image in the Responses API).
fieldDescription.has_audio: Match requests whose body contains at least one audio block (input_audio in chat completions or the Responses API).
fieldDescription.has_file: Match requests whose body contains at least one file block (file in chat completions, input_file in the Responses API).
fieldDescription.image_count: Route by the number of image blocks in the request body.
fieldDescription.audio_count: Route by the number of audio blocks in the request body.
fieldDescription.file_count: Route by the number of file blocks in the request body.
fieldDescription.headers: Match on an incoming HTTP request header. Use lowercase header names.
fieldDescription.params: Match on a query string parameter of the request URL.
fieldDescription.tokens_used: Check token usage as percentage. Checked against max of model and provider configs.
fieldDescription.request: Check request usage as percentage. Checked against max of model and provider configs.
fieldDescription.budget_used: Check budget usage as percentage. Checked against max of model and provider configs.

infoPopover.chainRule: On match, re-evaluate other routing rules using the chosen provider/model as input. Useful for chaining model aliasing with model-specific routing.
infoPopover.priority: Lower numbers run first. 0 is the highest priority. Ties keep source order.
infoPopover.targets: Weight is the share of requests sent to this provider/model. Sum must equal 1. Leave provider/model blank to keep the incoming value.
infoPopover.fallbacks: Tried in order when every target fails. Provider is required; model is optional.

validation.title: Fix the following before saving:
validation.scopeRequired: Pick an API key for the Virtual Key scope.
validation.weightPositive: Every target weight must be greater than 0.
validation.targetRequired: Add at least one routing target.

infoSheet.chainRuleTooltip: After this rule matches, routing rules are re-evaluated using the resolved provider/model as the new context.
infoSheet.testCommandDesc: Copy this command and run it to test routing for this rule

tree.title: Routing Tree
tree.pageDescription: Read-only decision tree visualization of routing rules
tree.staticChainTooltip: Re-entry point is fully proven by static analysis; every condition on the path evaluated to a known value.
tree.dynamicChainTooltip: Re-entry point is a conditional; one or more conditions on the path are not fully evaluated at build time.
tree.chainRuleDescription: Chain rule: resolved provider/model feeds back as the new input and the full scope chain re-evaluates.

complexityRouter.title: Complexity Router
complexityRouter.description: Route requests based on complexity tiers
complexityRouter.headerDescription: Tune how incoming requests are classified into four tiers. Thresholds and keyword lists feed the
complexityRouter.headerDescriptionSuffix: field that routing rules can target.
complexityRouter.keywordListsDescription: Lowercased and deduplicated on save. Each list requires at least one entry.
complexityRouter.typeKeywordPlaceholder: Type a keyword and press Enter
complexityRouter.restoreDefaultsDescription: This will reset all tier boundaries and keyword lists to the factory defaults. Your current configuration will be lost. This action cannot be undone.
complexityRouter.configUnavailable: No complexity router configuration is available.

validation.mustBeGreaterThanSimpleMedium: Must be greater than Simple → Medium
validation.mustBeGreaterThanMediumComplex: Must be greater than Medium → Complex
validation.simpleKeywordsDescription: Phrases that bias the request toward the SIMPLE tier (greetings, trivia, small talk).
validation.codeKeywordsDescription: Signals that the request involves code, debugging, or programming artifacts.
validation.technicalKeywordsDescription: Architecture, infra, and operational terms that raise the complexity score.
validation.reasoningKeywordsDescription: Strong reasoning triggers. Matching these phrases can override tier selection toward the REASONING tier.
validation.simpleAbove: Scores at or below this are classified as SIMPLE.
validation.mediumAbove: Scores above simple_medium and at or below this are MEDIUM.
validation.complexAbove: Scores above this are REASONING. Everything in between is COMPLEX.
